examples.title: Basic schedule builder
examples.description: Choose how a schedule repeats, the time it runs at and its time zone. The read-back sentence and the next runs stay visible whichever choice is showing.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ScheduleBuilder, type ScheduleFire, type ScheduleValue } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  let value = $state<ScheduleValue>({ cron: '0 9 * * 1-5', timeZone: 'America/Los_Angeles' });

  // Cinder ships no date math — a real app would bring its own cron library here.
  // Labels are illustrative static strings, not computed dates.
  function computeNextFires(current: ScheduleValue, count: number): ScheduleFire[] {
    const cadence =
      'every' in current ? `every ${current.every.count} ${current.every.unit}` : current.cron;
    return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
      id: `fire-${index}`,
      label: `Fire ${index + 1} — ${cadence}`,
    }));
  }

  function handleChange(next: ScheduleValue): void {
    value = next;
  }
</script>

<ScheduleBuilder {value} onValueChange={handleChange} {computeNextFires} label="Data sync schedule" />

examples.title: Custom cron
examples.description: Custom cron is the escape hatch for a schedule no other choice produces. Each of the five fields has a structured editor with an inline error, and an invalid expression is never emitted.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ScheduleBuilder, type ScheduleFire, type ScheduleValue } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  // A step restarts at midnight, so it opens as Custom cron rather than as an interval.
  let value = $state<ScheduleValue>({ cron: '0 */6 * * *', timeZone: 'UTC' });

  // Cinder ships no date math — a real app would bring its own cron library here.
  // Labels are illustrative static strings, not computed dates.
  function computeNextFires(current: ScheduleValue, count: number): ScheduleFire[] {
    const cadence =
      'every' in current ? `every ${current.every.count} ${current.every.unit}` : current.cron;
    return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
      id: `fire-${index}`,
      label: `Fire ${index + 1} — ${cadence}`,
    }));
  }

  function handleChange(next: ScheduleValue): void {
    value = next;
  }
</script>

<ScheduleBuilder {value} onValueChange={handleChange} {computeNextFires} label="Report job schedule" />

examples.title: Every few minutes or hours
examples.description: An interval counts from the start of the schedule, so an uneven one such as every 7 hours is exact. It emits an every value rather than a cron, and At is hidden.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ScheduleBuilder, type ScheduleFire, type ScheduleValue } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  let value = $state<ScheduleValue>({
    every: { unit: 'hours', count: 7 },
    timeZone: 'UTC',
  });

  // Cinder ships no date math — a real app would bring its own cron library here.
  // Labels are illustrative static strings, not computed dates.
  function computeNextFires(current: ScheduleValue, count: number): ScheduleFire[] {
    const cadence =
      'every' in current ? `every ${current.every.count} ${current.every.unit}` : current.cron;
    return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
      id: `fire-${index}`,
      label: `Fire ${index + 1} — ${cadence}`,
    }));
  }

  function handleChange(next: ScheduleValue): void {
    value = next;
  }
</script>

<ScheduleBuilder {value} onValueChange={handleChange} {computeNextFires} label="Health check schedule" />
